chunks: And with this chain, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ibn Muskan, from Abi Basir, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to me: 'If they deceive you about something, do not let them deceive you about Asr; pray it while the sun is clear. Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who wastes [his prayer] loses his family and his wealth.'
I asked: 'And who is the one who loses his family and wealth?' He replied: 'He will have neither family nor wealth in Paradise.'
I asked: 'And what is its wasting?' He replied: 'He leaves it, by Allah, until the sun turns yellow [at sunset] or sets.'

key_terms.تَصْفَرَّ الشَّمْسُ: The sun turns yellow (sign of late afternoon/sunset)

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of wasting the Asr prayer and its consequence in Paradise?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Thawab al-A'mal*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) elucidates the concept of *al-mawtur* (one who is cut off or deprived) as the specific individual who neglects the Asr prayer until the sun yellows or sets. This highlights the severe spiritual consequence of missing the 'time of the sun's clarity,' where the believer is deprived of their family and wealth in Paradise, emphasizing the critical importance of timely prayer in Shia jurisprudence.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 3. And from the previous chain from Muhammad b. Ali al-Kufi from Ali b. al-Nu’man from Ibn Muskan from Abi Basir who said:
a person who wastes Asr Prayer will be without relatives and wealth.”
The narrator asked, “Who is one without relatives and wealth?” Imam (a.s.) replied, “He is one who has neither any relatives nor any wealth in Paradise.”
The narrator asked, “What is meant by wasting Salaat?” Imam (a.s.) replied, “It means not offering it during the time between noon and sunset.”
